title: The Harbor of the Old Mill House
premise: Casper Voss, a widowed single father running the last bookshop in the fading harbor town of Millbrook, agrees to a fake date with a stranger to survive his family's reunion — only to discover she is Elena Marsh, the daughter of the developer whose company is buying out the waterfront, including his shop. Their staged romance deepens into something real even as Elena secretly holds the power to save or destroy the harbor, and Casper must finally speak the apology he has rehearsed for ten years since the night his wife died. When the demolition order arrives, Elena chooses love and truth over her father's empire, testifying against the project; the old mill house is saved as a community library, and Casper and Elena build their second chance on honest ground.
about_author: Marguerite Crane is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who spent fifteen years watching small harbors disappear beneath new money. She writes romances about people who arrive too late and stay anyway.

chapters.title: Salt on the Windows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He closes the bookshop early, dodging a notice from Marsh Development taped to his door, and tucks his daughter June into bed above the store. The beat is quiet dread: the harbor he loves is being priced out from under him.

chapters.title: The Reunion Letter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. His mother's summons to the Voss family reunion arrives with a pointed question about 'bringing someone.' Ten years of grief and one rehearsed sentence haunt him. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Counter
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. She wanders into the bookshop escaping her father's shadow, buying a novel she'll never read. Casper mistakes her for a tourist; she lets him. Beat: two people lying by omission, feeling seen anyway.

chapters.title: The Proposition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over coffee, Casper blurts an absurd offer: be my date to the reunion. Elena, needing cover from her father's surveillance of her weekend, says yes before thinking. Beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. They invent a history in the bookshop after hours — how they met, why it works. Every invented detail lands too close to truth. Beat: laughter curdling into vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Harbor Road
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Driving to the reunion along the coast, he shows her the old mill house ruins where he proposed to his late wife. Elena recognizes the site from her father's blueprints and says nothing. Beat: guilt planted.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the reunion, the fake date feels real by dessert — hands touching under the table, June adoring Elena. Then Casper's brother mentions Marsh Development by name, and Elena's face goes white. Beat: the lie begins to cost.

chapters.title: What She Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. She slips away and calls her father, learning the mill house demolition is scheduled within weeks. She returns wearing a smile like armor. Beat: complicity.

chapters.title: June's Map
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. June draws a crayon map of the harbor marking places she loves, including the mill house, and gives it to Elena. Elena keeps it in her briefcase next to the buyout contracts. Beat: innocence versus paperwork.

chapters.title: The Second Date
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A real, unplanned date at the lighthouse — no audience, no pretext. They almost kiss; Elena pulls back, terrified of what honesty would require. Beat: longing restrained.

chapters.title: Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Her father reveals he knows about the bookseller and orders her to use the relationship to get Casper's signature cheaply. She refuses; he threatens to expose her role in the project. Beat: power corrupting family.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the mill house at dusk, he begins the sentence rehearsed for a decade — an apology to his dead wife for surviving — but stops when Elena's phone lights up with her father's name. Beat: interrupted confession.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. She copies the demolition file, the forged easement, the bribed council votes — enough to burn the project down, and her family with it. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A rival developer mails Casper photos of Elena at board meetings. He confronts her in the empty shop; she admits everything except that she loves him. Beat: heartbreak with the door left ajar.

chapters.title: Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He boxes the shop's inventory, telling himself it was always coming. June asks if Elena is coming back, and he cannot answer. Beat: grief repeating itself.

chapters.title: The Council Meeting
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Marsh Development presents its final approval. Elena walks in uninvited, lays the forged documents on the table, and testifies against her own father. Beat: the climax of courage.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The vote stalls pending investigation; her father disowns her publicly. Casper watches the news in the dark shop, torn between fury and the memory of dessert. Beat: ruin and respect entangled.

chapters.title: Rain on the Mill House
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He finds Elena soaked at the mill house ruins. She says the sentence for him — that she should have told him from the first day — and he finally finishes his decade-old apology aloud. Beat: mutual absolution.

chapters.title: What the Town Decides
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The investigation voids the easements; the town proposes restoring the mill house as a library, with the bookshop as its anchor. Casper must decide whether to trust the town — and her — again. Beat: cautious rebuilding.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He signs the lease for the mill house library wing, then drives to Elena's hotel with June's crayon map framed in his arms. Beat: choosing again, eyes open.

chapters.title: The Harbor of the Old Mill House
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Opening day: shelves carried across the harbor road, June cutting the ribbon, Elena's hand in Casper's. Her father watches from a car and does not come in. Beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. One year later, above the library, Casper proposes where he once proposed before — and this time the sentence is not an apology but a promise. Elena says yes before he finishes. Beat: timing, finally right.
